item.title: Do women control their husbands?
item.description: By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing. In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work her way into her husband’s heart through his stomach. Women were traditionally expected to be seen but not heard. They were like shadows trailing their husbands, with little or no opportunity to express opinions on matters affecting the family and society. They were often regarded as acquired possessions whose primary responsibilities were to bear children and provide labour on the farms. They had little or no say in the scheme of things. A similar pattern appears in some biblical accounts, where headcounts excluded women and children. When Jesus fed the 5,000 and the 4,000, the recorded figures referred to the men, with women and children excluded from the count. In the early Christian community, Paul’s instruction required women to remain silent in church and ask their husbands questions at home. Although interpretations of this passage differ among Christian scholars, it has historically been cited to support restrictions on women’s public religious participation. Despite these historical and cultural limitations, women have, in different ways, exercised considerable influence over men, including their husbands. Biblical accounts The Bible contains several accounts of women whose actions, decisions or influence significantly shaped the lives of men. Eve persuaded Adam to eat the forbidden fruit after the serpent tempted her in the Garden of Eden. Jezebel manipulated her husband, King Ahab, and orchestrated the murder of Naboth to acquire his vineyard. Delilah used persistent pressure and deception to make Samson reveal the secret of his extraordinary strength. Sapphira conspired with her husband, Ananias, to deceive the apostles about the proceeds from the sale of their property. Michal helped David escape from King Saul but later confronted and despised him over his public dancing before God. Bathsheba, working alongside the prophet Nathan, intervened to ensure that David fulfilled his promise that Solomon would succeed him as king. Sarah persuaded Abraham to have a child through her maidservant, Hagar, and later demanded that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away. Rebekah orchestrated a family deception by persuading her son Jacob to disguise himself as Esau and obtain Isaac’s blessing. Herodias influenced her daughter to demand the head of John the Baptist from her husband, Herod Antipas. Job’s wife, overwhelmed by their suffering, urged her husband to curse God and die. Mary and Martha also demonstrated the emotional influence women could have. When their brother, Lazarus, died, their grief deeply moved Jesus, who wept before raising him from the dead. item.title: Infantino hails Warri Stadium, wants football in every community
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has praised the renovated Warri City Stadium in Delta State, saying football development must extend beyond major stadiums to local communities. Infantino spoke during a visit to Warri, where he attended the commissioning of the renovated stadium and upgraded sporting facilities. The FIFA president said football should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their location, adding that smaller stadiums play an important role in bringing the sport closer to communities. “Yeah, that’s what football is about, isn’t it? It’s for everyone, everywhere,” Infantino told reporters in Warri yesterday. “It’s big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also smaller stadiums. It’s the proximity, and to be here in Warri for me is a fantastic occasion to showcase what we are about in FIFA, what we are about in football.” Infantino also expressed appreciation for the warm reception he received in Nigeria and across Africa, attributing the relationship to years of collaboration and football development projects aimed at improving the lives of young people. “Oh yes, I’m feeling so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. This is based, of course, on many years of joint life together, of projects that we’ve put in place, of changing lives of girls and boys,” he said. item.title: Lagos renews campaign against open defecation
item.description: …Calls for improved sanitation, gender-sensitive toilet facilities By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has renewed its campaign for improved sanitation, proper hygiene practices and access to safe toilet facilities as part of efforts to eliminate open defecation and promote public health. The Special Adviser to the Governor on Environment, Olakunle Akodu, and the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources, Tajudeen Gaji, made the call on Friday as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate World Toilet Day at Alausa, Ikeja. The 2026 celebration was held under the theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality.” Akodu said women and girls required toilet facilities that guaranteed adequate privacy, reliable water supply, handwashing stations and hygienic conditions. He noted that Lagos’ growing population, rapid urbanisation and expanding commercial activities had placed enormous pressure on existing sanitation infrastructure. According to him, addressing the challenges requires deliberate public policies, sustained capital investment, institutional discipline and collective civic responsibility. He said the state government recognised that a clean, resilient and sustainable environment must guarantee every resident access to safe, dignified and functional sanitation facilities. Earlier, Gaji, who was represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Hassan Sanuth, said the commemoration underscored the importance of proper sanitation in preventing diseases, protecting public health and promoting a cleaner environment. He described access to safe toilets as more than a basic necessity, saying it was fundamental to human dignity and public health. Gaji said sanitation was closely linked to personal security, social equality and the fundamental right of every citizen to live in a healthy environment. He warned that inadequate access to safe and private toilet facilities could undermine people’s health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities. The permanent secretary therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that would address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. item.title: Waste crisis: LAWMA acting MD unveils 60-day action plan
item.description: …Warns staff against laxity, promises operational overhaul By Olasunkanmi Akoni The newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), Olajuwon Akinyemi, has unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to tackle waste management challenges across Lagos State, warning staff against indiscipline and poor performance. Akinyemi, who has assumed office amid growing concerns over waste accumulation across the metropolis, said the plan was aimed at clearing waste backlogs, strengthening regulatory enforcement and restoring the agency’s operational efficiency. He disclosed this on Friday while addressing management and staff at a workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa, Lagos. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Kunle Adebiyi, the acting managing director called for renewed commitment, discipline and professionalism among workers. He said repositioning the agency would require active participation and dedication from personnel at all levels. “We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi said. Outlining the 60-day action plan, he said personnel would be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with the respective areas to strengthen field monitoring and improve response times. He also announced plans to establish decentralised operational hubs to improve supervision, facilitate faster interventions and address waste disposal blackspots across the state. On indiscriminate waste disposal, Akinyemi said the agency would intensify public enlightenment on waste sorting at source and responsible disposal practices. He said traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations and artisans would be mobilised to promote compliance with proper waste management practices. The acting managing director also called for stronger collaboration with Private Sector Participation (PSP) operators and urged residents to comply with approved waste collection tariffs to sustain service delivery. On staff welfare, Akinyemi assured workers that their well-being remained a priority, disclosing that efforts were underway to procure Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered buses to address transportation challenges. Earlier, Tijani called for urgent action to revitalise LAWMA’s operational framework, saying the agency needed an immediate overhaul to improve field performance. Similarly, Adebiyi said the success of the 60-day plan would depend on prudent financial management, accountability and effective collaboration across the agency’s directorates. item.title: Nefer introduces marketplace to make peer-to-peer currency exchange more secure for Nigerians
item.description: * The new feature allows users to buy and sell currencies with other users on the Nefer platform, with funds held in escrow during transactions. Nefer Remittance , a financial technology company facilitating payments and currency exchange between Nigeria and Canada, has introduced Nefer Marketplace, a new feature that enables users to buy and sell currencies directly with one another within its platform. The launch addresses a familiar challenge for Nigerians who regularly need foreign currencies for international payments, education, business transactions, travel and other financial commitments: finding reliable people to exchange money with. For many users, peer-to-peer currency exchange has traditionally happened through WhatsApp groups, social media communities and personal referrals. While these informal networks may offer access to buyers and sellers, they often lack structured transaction processes, adequate accountability and mechanisms for resolving disputes when transactions go wrong. Nefer Marketplace seeks to provide an alternative by bringing peer-to-peer currency trading into a structured digital environment. Unlike informal arrangements where buyers and sellers transfer funds directly to one another, Nefer Marketplace incorporates an escrow mechanism. Funds are held by Nefer during the transaction, providing an additional layer of protection while the parties complete the exchange in accordance with the platform’s transaction process. This means users do not have to rely solely on personal trust or the promises of an unknown seller when arranging a currency exchange. Making Currency Exchange More Accessible The introduction of Marketplace builds on Nefer’s existing services, which help customers move money between Nigeria and Canada. Through the Nefer app, users can maintain Naira and Canadian dollar wallets, convert Naira to Canadian dollars and make payments for different international needs, including Canadian school fees and vehicle-related transactions. With Marketplace, Nefer is extending this experience by giving users another way to access currency through peer-to-peer trading. For Nigerians who frequently make payments in Canada, including car importers, students, parents and businesses, access to a reliable currency exchange option can make a significant difference to how they manage their international financial commitments. Beyond Informal Currency Trading The growth of digital communities has made it easier for people to find individuals willing to exchange currencies. However, accessibility does not always translate to security. Transactions arranged through informal groups can leave participants exposed to failed transfers, unresponsive counterparties and difficulties establishing accountability. By introducing an escrow-supported marketplace within its app, Nefer is bringing greater structure to a process that has largely operated through informal networks. item.title: Nwobodo urges ESUT to prioritise innovation, research, good governance
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—-Former Governor of old Anambra State and former Minister of Sports, Chief (Dr.) Jim Ifeanyichukwu Nwobodo, has urged the Enugu State University of Science and Technology (ESUT) to prioritise research, technological innovation, entrepreneurship and good governance to enhance its contribution to national development. Nwobodo made the call while delivering the 3rd Distinguished Personality Lecture of ESUT during the university’s Special Convocation Ceremony at its permanent site at Ebe-ano City, Enugu State. The lecture was titled, “From Vision to Legacy: Technology, Education, Leadership, Good Governance and the Responsibility of a New Generation.” Nwobodo, who founded the Anambra State University of Science and Technology (ASUTECH) in 1980, said the establishment of the institution was a deliberate investment in the future, driven by the conviction that education, scientific knowledge, technological competence and visionary leadership were essential to societal progress. He expressed satisfaction with the growth of the university, noting that the institution’s continued development more than four decades after its establishment demonstrated the enduring value of its founding vision. According to him, the true measure of leadership goes beyond achievements recorded while in office to include the institutions established and the opportunities created for future generations. Reflecting on his experience in public service, Nwobodo said governments and political office holders might come and go, but institutions founded on sound principles and sustained through responsible governance could endure for generations. He stressed that visionary leadership required the courage to make difficult decisions and undertake initiatives whose benefits might extend beyond one’s tenure in public office. On the future of ESUT, the former governor called for its transformation into a leading centre for research, innovation, entrepreneurship, technological development and practical solutions to societal challenges. He said the university’s success should not be measured solely by student enrolment and graduation figures but also by the quality of its research, technological discoveries, entrepreneurial achievements and contributions to national development. Nwobodo advocated increased investment in applied research, urging engineering students to develop solutions to energy and infrastructure challenges, agricultural scientists to improve food production, medical researchers to advance healthcare, and computer scientists to develop applications in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and digital technology. He also called for stronger collaboration among students of management, law, economics and social sciences and their counterparts in science and engineering to translate research findings into commercially viable enterprises. item.title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
item.description: By Dickson Omobola African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said. He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems. Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment. item.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.” The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: [VIDEO] I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. item.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
item.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. item.title: I’m The Most Transparent, Vilified But I Shall Be Vindicated — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has expressed confidence that he will eventually be vindicated over the allegations of financial misconduct levelled against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). He also described himself as the most transparent individual. “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated,” Bello said on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday. ﻿ When asked to respond to allegations of financial mismanagement while in government, the former governor urged people in doubt to go to the state and ask questions about how resources were managed. He said he pities those who call him a thief. The former governor also described himself as a man who was blessed by God and able to meet his needs and those of his family members. Bello, who has consistently denied wrongdoing, is facing multiple cases instituted by the anti-graft agency over alleged misappropriation of public funds during his eight-year tenure as governor of the state. The EFCC Chairman, Ola Olukoyede, said in an interview with Channels Television in January 2026 that the commission had filed three cases against the former governor and fulfilled its mandate by investigating and prosecuting him. According to Olukoyede, the responsibility for determining Bello’s guilt rests with the judiciary. One of the cases involves a 16-count charge bordering on alleged criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving ₦110.4 billion. Bello, who was the governor from 2016 to 2024, is standing trial alongside two former state government officials. The Federal Government alleges that the defendants diverted state funds to acquire properties in highbrow areas of Abuja and Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Bello is also facing a separate 19-count charge involving an alleged ₦80.2 billion fraud and money laundering before the Federal High Court in Abuja. However, some prosecution witnesses have given evidence that has featured prominently in the proceedings. In February 2026, an EFCC witness, Olomotane Egoro, told the Federal High Court that Bello’s name did not appear as a beneficiary, signatory, or party to transactions involving some companies allegedly awarded local government contracts in Kogi State. Similarly, in March, another prosecution witness, Mahmoud Abdulazeez, maintained that Bello’s name was not linked to the transactions involving property documents tendered before the court. In June 2026, the 17th prosecution witness, Shehu Bala, also told the court during cross-examination that Bello was not involved in the property transactions under examination. item.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
item.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. While Tekenah has leaned into her local roots, the coffee industry has also been helped by a growing sense of cosmopolitanism in Nigeria’s cities, Ali said.
